title: Refine kernel dispatch and prefill->decode pipeline for H100/L40S/A10 under MIG and dynamic clocking
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We've observed variable throughput and bursty p95 latency across H100/L40S/A10 fleets depending on MIG partitioning and active GPU clocks. Two major contributors identified: (1) suboptimal kernel selection when sequence-length distributions diverge between prefill and decode phases, and (2) prefill/decode scheduling that fails to exploit cross-request KV cache reuse while respecting latency SLOs. Goal: Implement a hardware-aware kernel dispatch heuristic + prefill->decode pipeline adjustments that improve tokens/sec and p95 latency consistency across MIG partitions and when GPUs are in different clock modes. Success metrics: (a) +12% median tokens/sec on average across H100/L40S/A10 for common conversational workloads; (b) p95 latency regression <= 5% for interactive routes; (c) end-to-end cost-per-token reduced by >= 10% on targeted workloads; (d) stable behavior across 1/2/7-way MIG splits.

Scope and constraints: Work targets runtime kernel selection layer and scheduler only. No model architecture changes. Must maintain correctness (bit-identical outputs) and preserve current API compatibility. Some tactics (e.g., forcing clocks) require cooperation with infra / cloud partner for safety.

Planned approach:
- Instrument: Add per-request sequence-length histogram tagging and GPU clock/mig metadata in trace context so routing heuristic has visibility. (Telemetry PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/4123)
- Heuristic: Build a kernel dispatch policy that prefers fused/multihead kernels for long-prefill short-decode patterns and lightweight kernels for short-prefill long-decode patterns. Policy is weighted by measured per-model sequence distribution and a small hardware profile (SM count, MIG slices, peak SM clocks).
- Prefill/Decode pipeline: Introduce a soft prefetch stage for KV cache when requests likely to reuse prefixes across active sessions, and allow temporary micro-batching of decode steps (windowed 1-3 token micro-batches) when that reduces kernel launch overhead without blowing interactive latency.
- Clocking: Add safe integrations for reading current GPU clock states and prefer kernel variants tuned for the observed clock. Evaluate a non-invasive option: kernel variant selection (fast vs. stable) rather than forcing clock changes.
- Autotune: Run short experiments that sweep kernel variant selection thresholds per-device type and persist tuned thresholds in the model profile store.

Acceptance criteria (QA):
- Bench harness reproduces improved tokens/sec on H100, L40S, and A10 with at least 3 representative prompts each (chatty, short-answer, long-context). Measurement code added to perf dashboard.
- Canary on dedicated capacity with conservative rollout (10% traffic) and fallback to previous kernel policy on metric regressions.
- Documentation: Add a runtime-1.22 note describing heuristic and ops playbook for disabling when necessary.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Micro-batching decode harms tail latency for some interactive customers. Mitigation: Conservative default thresholds (max 3-token micro-batches) and feature flag gated per-route.
- Risk: Inaccurate heuristics for uncommon sequence distributions. Mitigation: Fall back to legacy kernel selection when confidence low and log for offline analysis.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/HW-aware+kernel+dispatch
- Perf PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4123
- Benchmark dashboard: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/runtime/hw-kernel-select

Notes: engineering, infra, and solutions-eng alignment required before enabling clock-manipulation knobs in production.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Ava Martinez: Initial triage complete. Performance owner assigned to Samir. Mapped affected routes and sample models (gpt-small-chat, redwood-internal-sft).

2026-02-18 - Samir Patel: Added sequence-length tagging to traces; telemetry confirms bimodal distribution on chatty routes (prefill > decode vs prefill ~ decode). Note: L40S shows more sensitivity to kernel launch overhead than H100.

2026-02-25 - Elena Zhou (Infra): Observed that some cloud nodes had dynamic clock changes during noisy-neighbor events. Suggested reading clock only for decision-making, not forcing clocks in first pass.

2026-02-28 - Samir Patel: Experiment #1 (fused-kernel preference for long-prefill pattern) deployed to benchmark runners. Baseline tokens/sec H100 (single stream): 4.2k -> fused: 5.1k (+21%); L40S baseline 3.0k -> fused 3.5k (+16%); A10 baseline 1.8k -> fused 2.0k (+11%). Latency p95 unchanged for H100/L40S, slight p95 +3% for A10 under high contention. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4189
2026-03-03 - Marcus Lee (SRE): Canary plan approved for dedicated fleet. Ops runbook drafted: rollback via KMD flag and extra telemetry retention for 48h.

2026-03-07 - Samir Patel: Experiment #2 (micro-batching decode with confidence threshold) shows reduced CPU->GPU kernel overhead and improved aggregate throughput in bursty traffic; however, interactive tail for some short-turn routes regressed by ~6% p95. Decided to gate micro-batching behind per-route flag. Issue created to expose flag in console for customers.

2026-03-10 - Design review requested: reduced description of heuristic and policy knobs. Design feedback from UX: surface 'kernel policy' in per-model profile page with simple on/off and 'aggressive' slider.

2026-03-12 - Samir Patel: Rollout to 10% traffic on Dedicated H100 fleet started. Early metrics: tokens/sec +13% overall on test routes, customer_impact metric stable. Next: run extended 72h stability and add MIG split-specific tuning for 7-way partitions.
